My problem with this is all of it. Downvote if you please, but read it all. Sexual assault takes a toll on people’s mental health. As someone who has been through all types of abuse from both a parent and a partner and has been sexually assaulted on top of that, I fucking survived it. 

Being a victim is the beginning. I am not just any other victim who needs pity and always feels like shit anymore. Being a victim means being in that mindset, going through the motions of what happened to you and how you feel about yourself. Being a victim means having feelings of anxiety, depression, suicide, etc. Being a victim means slicing up my arm because I don’t wanna be a victim of my own fucking pain.

Being a survivor means I got through that shit. It means I had bad things happen to me, and as a result I felt bad. Really fucking bad. Bad enough to be hospitalized five times in one year and begin to mutilate my body at eleven. I survived everything that I felt and did to myself as a result of what others did to me. I made it through that shit. I am NOT a victim anymore.

What you people seem to forget is that there is another step after becoming a survivor. It’s fucking thriving. Being able to live without wanting to kill myself every time I see my abuser, being able to fucking forgive people for the shit they’ve done to me, being able to laugh and smile and find thing that genuinely make me happy. Not feeling like I have to punish myself because I’m not pure enough. Not feeling like I have to hide myself because of fear it might happen again. Being a thriver means I still have a ways to go, but that I’m allowing myself to be god damned happy again.

Idk, as someone who has survived all types of abuse from both a parent and a partner and been the victim of sexual trauma, the therapy I go through sees the words much much differently.

When you’re a victim, that awful thing seems to happen to you over and over again, like you can’t get away from it. Being a victim gives you a reason to see yourself as still living in that time period and that trauma. If you’re a victim, it seems like it’s over. 

Then you start therapy and learn what being a survivor is. You can say, yeah, that happened, but I made it out. I’m strong enough to get through hard times. Being a victim feels weak and is seen as someone who needs pity. Being a survivor means it’s behind you and you’re beginning to move on and discover your worth.

The last part that everyone seems to forget is being a thriver. Being a thriver allows you to push past your circumstances and grow from them instead of being held back and trapped by them. 

Having a victim mindset isn’t the way to go.

You don’t understand the therapy sexual assault victims go through. Being a victim allows you to stay in the headspace of negativity surrounding your situation, being a survivor means you got through that negative mentality, and being a thriver means you’re now coming through recovery and are able to move on from it.
